What is Infinite Magicraid?

Infinite Magicraid (IMR) is a turn-based tactical RPG with idle elements. You collect heroes, build teams of five around their skills, and fight through PvE content, PvP arenas and guild wars. It is a gacha game: most heroes come from summons (Wishes), so luck plays a part in what you own.

More than anything, IMR is a resource management game. Resources are limited, and the game constantly tempts you to spend them on things that feel good now but don't move your account forward. Players who plan and spend efficiently pull ahead, and free-to-play is viable with the right mindset and realistic expectations.

LTEs vs Legendaries

Heroes come in several rarities: Epic, Legendary, LTE (Limited Time Event) and Mythic. The two that matter most for planning are Legendaries and LTEs.

LegendaryLTE
PowerStrong; the newest ones shape the metaThe strongest heroes in the game
ReleaseMiracle Wish bannerMiracle Wish banner
After releaseJoins the Normal Wish pool after 2 weeks and returns on bannersLimited. Returns on the “Hero Rate +” banner after about a year
Raising ExclusivesHero copies, or Legendary Dragon Eyes for top-tier heroesHero copies only

Exclusives (E levels)

Each extra copy of a hero raises its Exclusive level. E3 (4 copies) is the big power spike and the goal for any hero you plan to use seriously. A hero at E3 is considered “fully activated”.

LTE rules (Bougatsa’s Wisdom): use Diamonds to buy Miracle Runes. Only spend Miracles to take a new LTE to E3. It is OK to skip an LTE you can’t E3.

Prioritization

The most common mistake is spreading resources across many heroes. Pick a direction and finish it.

Long-term goals, in order

  1. E3 new LTEs
  2. E3 older LTEs
  3. E3 new Legendaries
  4. E3 older Legendaries

Short-term gains (feel good, small impact)

  • Awakening heroes to A5 or levelling to 150
  • Enhancing equipment
  • Raising older, off-meta Legendaries
Do not sacrifice long-term goals for short-term gains.

Rules of thumb

  • Upgrade one hero at a time. A finished DPS beats five half-built heroes.
  • Awakening (A1–A5, Lv110–150): do your main damage dealers first.
  • Breakthrough (BT1–BT8, Lv155–190): LTEs and top-tier Legendaries first.
  • Legendary Dragon Eyes are extremely rare. Only use them on new, meta Legendaries rated A tier or higher in the tier list.
  • Spirit Beasts and Arcane Gems are power layers on top of your heroes; build heroes first. See Spirit Beasts and Arcane Gems.

Resource management

Almost everything comes back to a few currencies. Know what each one is for before you spend it.

ResourceWhat it's forAdvice
Miracle RunesSummoning new LTEs and new LegendariesSave them. E3 on a new LTE costs about 1,800 (450 per copy). Never gamble Miracles.
DiamondsThe main premium currencyConvert to Miracle Runes in the Resource Store (always 150 Diamonds each).
Excellent / Supreme RunesNormal summons and LTE rerunsConvert to Echo summons at a pace you can sustain. Always save enough for 2× Legendary. Supremes should be used only for targeted LTE reruns.
Echo WishPower-scaling mechanicSave for new LTEs.
Dragon EyesRaising Legendary Exclusives without copies10 Epic Dragon Eyes = 1 Legendary Dragon Eye. Only on A-tier+ meta Legendaries.

Saving beats pulling

Players who summon every time they get a few Miracles rarely finish a hero. Players who save until they can guarantee an E3 on a targeted LTE progress much faster. The F2P loop is Save → Wait → Summon during strong events (such as 2× Legendary or Gift of Heaven).

Spending, if you choose to

The best value for every spender is the same base: Monthly Card, Battle Pass, Championship Pass and Epic Eye packs. Beyond that, put money toward LTE copies to reach E3 before anything else.

Bougatsa’s Wisdom: never count on luck. Use resources only when ready. Upgrade one hero at a time. Ask questions if unsure.
